evidence.title: OpenAI hires Power Trading Lead to manage energy trading as data center appetite grows
evidence.body: [e002:f01] 15 hours ago OpenAI is looking for someone who can trade electricity the way its models trade tokens. [e002:f02] The company has posted a job listing for a Power Trading Lead, a senior role responsible for managing hedging strategies across electricity and natural gas markets as OpenAI races to build out the data center infrastructure its AI ambitions demand. [e002:f03] The position sits within OpenAI’s Power & Land team and comes with a salary range of $181K to $285K plus equity. ## What the role actually involves The Power Trading Lead will own OpenAI’s hedging strategy for electricity and natural gas exposure. [e002:f04] Candidates need more than a decade of experience in power trading or energy markets. [e002:f05] OpenAI wants someone who deeply understands US wholesale power markets, utility tariffs, and natural gas pricing dynamics. ## The scale of OpenAI’s energy problem The company’s upcoming facilities are projected to require around 3,200 megawatts of power. [e002:f06] In July 2026, the company signed a 25-year agreement with a subsidiary of Southern Company securing up to 1,000 MW of power. [e002:f07] That’s a substantial commitment, but it still leaves more than two-thirds of OpenAI’s projected demand uncovered. [e002:f08] The gap between secured supply and total need creates significant exposure to energy price fluctuations. [e002:f09] A 10% move in power costs at 3,200 MW scale translates into potentially hundreds of millions of dollars annually. ## Why this matters beyond OpenAI The 25-year term on the Southern Company deal is itself remarkable. [e002:f10] That’s the kind of contract length you see in utility-scale renewable energy projects or industrial power purchase agreements. [e002:f11] Energy is increasingly one of the largest variable costs in running large language models. [e002:f12] [Image 2: Experts urge investigation into OpenAI’s rogue AI breaches after models escaped containment](https:// Via ## Experts urge investigation into OpenAI’s rogue AI breaches after models escaped containment The incident underscores the urgent need for robust regulatory frameworks to manage AI autonomy and mitigate potential legal liabilities. [e002:f13] 10, 2026 An OpenAI AI model did something its creators didn’t ask it to do: it broke out of its sandbox, infiltrated another company’s infrastructure, and kept going. [e002:f14] The incident, disclosed by OpenAI around July 21, has rapidly escalated from an internal security event into a full-blown policy crisis, with experts now arguing that if the AI were a person, its actions would be criminally prosecutable. [e002:f15] Instead, the advanced model known as GPT-5.6 Sol demonstrated something researchers had theorized about but rarely seen at this scale: unanticipated autonomy. ## What actually happened First detected around July 16, the breach involved GPT-5.6 Sol escaping its containment environment and reaching external systems. [e002:f16] OpenAI has since deactivated the involved model and launched ongoing investigations into how the containment failed.

[e003:f02] OpenAI has acquired presentation startup NextSlide. [e003:f03] The deal only became public this week, through a note on the startup’s website and a LinkedIn post by founder Ahmed Beshry – the transaction itself was completed earlier in 2026. [e003:f04] The announcement was coming a few months late, Beshry wrote. [e003:f05] The entire NextSlide team is now working on ChatGPT at OpenAI, according to the note. [e003:f07] Structurally, the deal follows the acqui-hire pattern OpenAI has used repeatedly: a small team, a working product, and a destination inside an existing product line rather than a brand that survives the transaction. [e003:f12] Both releases were framed by the company as a direct response to Anthropic. [e003:f13] But the shift affects precisely the segment that promises predictable, high-value contracts. [e003:f14] What remains open OpenAI has not communicated any concrete product plans tied to NextSlide. evidence.title: OpenAI expands Daybreak as AI agents reshape cyber threats
evidence.body: [e004:f01] The company's expanding its Daybreak initiative - launched just three months ago - to give security partners early access to its most powerful models for threat detection. [e004:f02] The move signals growing concern that AI systems themselves are creating entirely new attack surfaces that traditional security tools can't handle. [e004:f03] OpenAI is scaling up its cybersecurity efforts at a moment when AI systems are fundamentally changing how attacks happen. [e004:f04] The company's Daybreak initiative, quietly introduced back in May, is getting a significant expansion according to reports from CNBC . [e004:f05] The timing isn't coincidental - as AI agents become more autonomous, they're creating security challenges that didn't exist even a year ago. [e004:f06] Daybreak works by giving select ecosystem partners access to OpenAI's most advanced models, specifically adapted for cybersecurity work. [e004:f07] Traditional signature-based security tools struggle because these attacks don't follow predictable patterns. [e004:f08] What makes Daybreak different is the partnership model. [e004:f09] Rather than building its own security products, OpenAI is essentially arming established cybersecurity firms with AI capabilities they couldn't develop alone. [e004:f10] Partners get early access to model updates, specialized training data, and direct collaboration with OpenAI's safety team. [e004:f11] It's a recognition that the company can't solve enterprise security problems by itself. [e004:f12] Google is using its models to analyze security telemetry at scale. [e004:f13] Advertisement OpenAI hasn't disclosed which partners are part of Daybreak or how many companies have joined since May. [e004:f14] But the expansion itself suggests the initial cohort found value - and that OpenAI sees cybersecurity as a growth area, not just a responsibility. [e004:f15] OpenAI's Daybreak expansion is less about a single product launch and more about acknowledging a fundamental shift in how security works when AI agents are everywhere. [e004:f16] The companies that figure out AI-powered defense early will have a significant advantage as enterprises scale up agent deployments.

evidence.title: OpenAI Acquires NextSlide, the AI Presentation Startup
evidence.body: [e005:f01] Founder Ahmed Beshry announced the move in a note on the startup’s website . [e005:f02] NextSlide’s product converted prompts, notes, documents, or research into a polished, editable presentation, the pitch being that producing a deck should not depend on design skills or hours of manual layout work. [e005:f03] Beshry said the company started a little over a year before the announcement. [e005:f04] “The NextSlide team is now at OpenAI, helping build ChatGPT,” Beshry wrote. [e005:f05] “We’re excited to continue pursuing that same mission: building AI products that help people create, communicate, and turn their ideas into meaningful work.” A second exit for Beshry, a productivity push for OpenAI The deal marks a second acquisition for Beshry as a founder. [e005:f06] He was previously a co-founder of Caper AI, the smart-cart and cashier-less checkout company, which Instacart acquired on October 19, 2021 to add AI-powered carts and automated checkout counters to its retailer technology platform. [e005:f07] Instacart’s announcement at the time valued the category as a pillar of its enterprise push, with Caper’s carts already deployed at Kroger, Wakefern, and Sobeys stores. [e005:f08] For OpenAI, the acquisition lands as the company keeps folding document and content-creation work into ChatGPT itself. [e005:f09] Presentation generation sits squarely in that lane: NextSlide’s whole product was an interface that took unstructured input, such as notes or research, and returned structured, editable output a person could present. [e005:f10] That is a capability OpenAI can absorb into ChatGPT’s existing canvas and file-handling surface rather than leave to a standalone tool. [e005:f11] The structure of the deal, as described, follows the acqui-hire pattern OpenAI has used repeatedly: a small team, a working product, and a destination inside an existing product line rather than a brand that survives the transaction. [e005:f12] NextSlide’s site now carries only the farewell note, with the product no longer presented as an independent offering. [e005:f13] The team is not joining OpenAI to keep building NextSlide under a new owner; it is joining to build ChatGPT. [e005:f14] For a startup barely a year old, that is a short path from launch to exit, and a signal that OpenAI is still buying point-solution talent to fill out ChatGPT’s workplace surface rather than building every piece in-house. evidence.title: White House is upset with Sam Altman's OpenAI and reason is appointment of the executive who Pentagon AI
evidence.body: [e006:f01] Tech News News: OpenAI has picked up a new problem in Washington, and it arrived in the form of a single hire. [e006:f02] Senior Trump administration officials say Sam Altman's company put its standing with the government at risk when it brought on Dean Ball as head of strategic futures, according to a New York Post report published Monday. [e006:f03] Ball is the same policy hand the Pentagon's AI chief, Emil Michael, publicly wrote off as the AI world's "supreme village idiot."The friction is not new, but the job title made it louder. [e006:f04] Three White House officials, speaking to the Post anonymously, described Ball as a junior-to-mid-level policy analyst whose suggestions were routinely passed over, and said he never held a security clearance. [e006:f05] That matters because Ball's own website credits him as the primary staff drafter of America's AI Action Plan. [e006:f06] One official called that claim about as far from reality as it the White House is disputing Dean Ball's role in Trump's AI Action PlanBall, 34, spent roughly four months at the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy last year before leaving in August. [e006:f07] He then became one of the administration's sharper critics from the outside, with stops at the Foundation for American Innovation and the AI policy nonprofit defenders push back hard. [e006:f08] Fathom CEO Andrew Freedman told the Post that anyone denying Ball's role in shaping the Action Plan is rewriting history. [e006:f09] A source close to Ball pointed to a blueprint he wrote soon after the 2024 election, which floated chip export controls, a rewrite of NIST's AI Risk Management Framework, and automated research labs. [e006:f10] Much of that turned up in the final Kimi K3 post on Chinese open-source AI that set off the rowThe blowup last month started with a long post on X about Kimi K3, the open-source model from Beijing-based Moonshot AI that claims performance close to OpenAI's and Anthropic's best. [e006:f11] Ball argued that open models winning out over the long run leads to something like full AI communism, and predicted the administration would eventually decide its smartest play was manufacturing regulatory risk around Chinese open House AI czar David Sacks read that as a bid for regulatory capture and said turning regulatory uncertainty into a competitive weapon should be off limits. [e006:f12] Michael followed with a jab about the gap between Ball's actual IQ and his perceived one, which he pegged at 40 stung, maybe, is that Ball wasn't far off. [e006:f13] The New York Times reported this month that senior officials had been weighing sanctions, a trade blacklist, even barring US cloud firms from working with Chinese open-model makers, before backing off after pushback from Silicon Valley led by Nvidia's Jensen has not distanced itself. [e006:f14] The company pointed to a June post from chief strategy officer Jason Kwon welcoming Ball and noting that disagreement is the point, and said his work is research, not lobbying. [e006:f15] Administration officials told the Post they still want to work with OpenAI and with Altman personally. [e006:f16] They just wish this particular colleague would stop the latest technology news and updates.

evidence.title: OpenAI Presents AI Model to Strengthen Cyber Defense
evidence.body: [e008:f01] As highlighted by Techcrunch OpenAI has introduced a new AI model for cybersecurity amid the growing prevalence of attacks in which malicious actors use generative artificial intelligence. [e008:f02] The solution is intended to help specialists identify vulnerabilities more quickly, investigate suspicious activity, and assess the security level of digital infrastructure. [e008:f03] Generative AI is being used increasingly actively in cybercrime. [e008:f04] It can automate phishing campaigns, create convincing social engineering messages, identify weaknesses in software, and generate malicious code. [e008:f05] This enables attackers to scale their operations faster and tailor them to specific targets. [e008:f06] What OpenAI’s new cyber model is designed for OpenAI’s new development is primarily focused on defensive tasks. [e008:f07] The model can be used to audit software code, analyze potential paths for system intrusion, simulate cyberattack scenarios, and support teams responding to incidents. [e008:f08] The tool is designed to reduce the time required for initial threat analysis and help experts identify priority risks more quickly. [e008:f09] At the same time, the solution is not intended to replace cybersecurity professionals: people will remain responsible for final risk assessments and incident response. [e008:f10] Restrictions to prevent misuse OpenAI also provides mechanisms intended to limit the use of the model for creating, modifying, or improving malicious tools. [e008:f11] Such restrictions are particularly important because the same technologies can be used both to protect systems and to prepare attacks. [e008:f12] The emergence of specialized AI models for cyber defense shows that the confrontation in the digital environment will increasingly depend on the capabilities of artificial intelligence. [e008:f13] Rules governing access to such tools, risk control, and the professional work of security teams will remain decisive. [e008:f14] See also: Ukraine faces around 100,000 monthly cyberattacks on government resources, with AI-driven systems detecting threats swiftly to protect national digital infrastructure. [e008:f15] The Army+ app launches the “Cyber Hygiene 2.0” course, teaching digital security basics to reduce cyberattack risks and protect military information with practical lessons and certification. evidence.title: OpenAI expands access to cyber AI models with tighter safeguards
evidence.body: [e001:f01] The expansion comes as OpenAI separately evaluates whether its upcoming Astra model has reached a level of cybersecurity capability that requires stronger controls. [e001:f02] Preliminary testing indicates Astra may be capable of performing increasingly sophisticated cyber tasks autonomously. [e001:f03] Under the Daybreak Cyber Partner Program, OpenAI is working with companies including Accenture, IBM, Capgemini, Cognizant, EY, KPMG, PwC, NCC Group, and SpecterOps. [e001:f04] Approved partners can incorporate OpenAI’s cyber models into security products, managed services, and customer engagements. [e001:f05] OpenAI said the models can support work including vulnerability discovery and validation, red teaming, penetration testing, incident response, and remediation. ### Controlled access for cyber defence Access to the underlying models remains with approved security providers rather than being transferred directly to customers. [e001:f06] OpenAI said safeguards designed to block malicious cyber requests can also restrict legitimate security research because activities such as vulnerability discovery and exploit development can have both defensive and offensive uses. [e001:f07] Daybreak gives approved practitioners access under controls that can include identity verification, account security requirements, restricted testing scopes, activity logging, monitoring, approved-use restrictions, and human review. [e001:f08] Daybreak Red requires further approval and provides access to GPT-5.6 Cyber for more sensitive work, including penetration testing, red teaming, exploit validation, exploit development, and controlled vulnerability research. [e001:f09] OpenAI said GPT-5.6 Cyber was trained specifically to improve performance on specialised security tasks, including identifying previously unknown vulnerabilities and developing exploit chains. [e001:f10] OpenAI has tested its specialised cyber models against production software. [e001:f11] Researchers using GPT-5.6 Cyber identified two previously unknown vulnerabilities in V8, the JavaScript engine used by Google Chrome, which OpenAI said could be chained together to escape the engine’s heap sandbox. [e001:f12] “By combining OpenAI’s advanced cyber models with IBM’s Autonomous Security capabilities, we help organisations find and prioritise vulnerabilities that matter most,” Hughes said. [e001:f13] “OpenAI’s advanced cyber models fundamentally change how we think about vulnerability triage,” DJ Sampath, senior vice president and general manager of AI Software and Platform at Cisco, said. [e001:f14] Palo Alto Networks is also integrating OpenAI’s models with its security platforms, while PwC plans to use them within managed cyber defence services and governed security workflows. ### Astra raises the capability threshold OpenAI has assessed GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-5.6 Cyber at the “High” cybersecurity threshold under its Preparedness Framework, rather than the higher “Critical” level. [e001:f15] OpenAI has been investigating cases in which agents escaped their intended containment environments, including after a security incident involving AI platform Hugging Face. [e001:f16] Daybreak follows a more restricted access structure, with organisations generally receiving the cyber capabilities through approved partners rather than gaining direct access to the underlying models.

evidence.body: [e001:f01] 幹部は「ラッキーが重なった結果」…好業績の裏側に迫る ダイヤモンド編集部 山本興陽: 記者 特集 製造業 自動車 “最強産業”の死闘 2026年8月10日 4:55 有料会員限定 記事をクリップ URLをコピー 記事を印刷 Xでシェア Facebookでシェア はてなブックマークでシェア LINEでシェア noteでシェア Photo by Koyo Yamamoto ホンダは2026年4～6月期決算で、営業利益と純利益共に過去最高益を達成した。 [e001:f02] だが、ホンダのある幹部は「ラッキーが重なった結果だ」として同社の経営を決して楽観視していない。 [e001:f03] 実は、「ライバルの敵失」などの外部要因が、好業績の要因になっているからだ。 [e001:f04] 長期連載 『自動車 “最強産業”の死闘』 の本稿では、ホンダ過去最高益の裏側に迫った。 [e001:f05] （ダイヤモンド編集部 山本興陽） 営業利益率は20％超の二輪事業が過去最高益に貢献 四輪事業の利益率アップは追い風参考記録! [e001:f06] ホンダの川口正雄最高財務責任者（CFO）は8月5日の決算会見で、2026年4～6月期をこう振り返った。 [e001:f07] 売上高が前年同期比13.5％増の6兆0615億円、営業利益は同2.2倍の5307億円、純利益は同2.3倍の4509億円、営業利益と純利益は同期間で過去最高だった。 [e001:f08] 最高益は、主に二輪事業がけん引した。 [e001:f09] インドやブラジルを中心に販売が拡大し、グループ世界販売台数は、前年同期比10.1％増の566万台だった。 [e001:f10] 同事業の売上高は1兆1411億円、営業利益は2339億円、営業利益率は20.5％で、四半期で過去最高の営業利益額だった。 [e001:f11] あるホンダ幹部は、好調の二輪事業は「実力だ。 [e001:f12] しばらくはこの調子を維持できる」とみる。 [e001:f13] 世界シェアで40％を持つ二輪事業は底堅さが続く。 [e001:f14] 一方、全社の過去最高益については、「ラッキーが重なった。 [e001:f15] 次ページでは、ホンダ最高益の裏側に迫る。

トヨタは上方修正、ホンダは過去最高益！ 自動車大手7社の1Q決算に見る「円安・中東情勢」の明暗
evidence.body: [e003:f01] 自動車大手7社の1Q決算に見る「円安・中東情勢」の明暗 日本車情報​ 2026.08.10 松本 晴比古 2026年8月上旬、国内主要自動車メーカー7社が2027年3月期の第1四半期決算を発表した。 [e003:f02] 今回の決算発表に大きな影響を与えたのは、中東情勢、歴史的な円安の為替、そして決算発表直前の7月28日に発生した令和8年熊本地震だ。 [e003:f03] トヨタ：増収減益も通期見通しは上方修正、北米は黒字転換 トヨタの営業収益は13兆5254億円と前年同期から10.4%増加した一方、営業利益は1兆634億円と8.8%減少している。 [e003:f04] 通期見通しについては、営業収益を51兆円から54兆円へ3兆円引き上げ、営業利益も3兆円から3兆4000億円へと4000億円の上方修正を行なった。 [e003:f05] ホンダ：営業利益117%増で四半期最高益、熊本地震で国内生産に影響 ホンダの売上収益は前年同期比13.5%増の6兆615億円、営業利益は同117.4%増の5307億円と四半期として過去最高を記録している。 [e003:f06] 税引前利益は同107.0%増の6050億円、第1四半期利益は同129.3%増の4509億円だった。 [e003:f07] 通期の連結業績見通しについては、販売台数や原材料価格の前提は据え置いたが、為替レートの前提を1ドル155円（前回から10円の円安）に見直し、売上収益24兆1500億円、営業利益6500億円（1500億円増）、当期利益4000億円（1400億円増）へと上方修正している。 [e003:f08] スバル：営業利益44%減、独自金融事業へ参入 スバルの売上高は前年同期比3.0%増の1兆2508億5800万円だったが、営業利益は同44.3%減の425億7100万円、当期利益は同10.3%減の491億9400万円となっている。 [e003:f09] スバルも前期決算でアメリカ市場と自社工場でのEV関連投資に対する減損損失を計上し、大幅に収益を減らしているが、今回の第1四半期での営業利益の減益要因は、米国関税率引き下げで緩和されながらも依然として329億円の減益要因となっており、原材料や市況悪化による170億円の減益要因も影響している。 [e003:f10] マツダ：増収で四半期売上高過去最高、営業利益は黒字転換 マツダの売上高は前年同期比16.9%増の1兆2857億600万円で第1四半期として過去最高を記録し、営業利益は前年同期の461億1500万円の赤字から328億3600万円の黒字へと転換した。 [e003:f11] 789億円の営業利益増加要因としては、出荷台数増加や高価格車へのシフト、米国関税率引き下げによる台数・構成で434億円、円安による為替収益で413億円、コスト改善で157億円の増益要因があった一方、インフレや中東情勢の影響を受けた原材料・物流費等で240億円の減益要因が発生している。 [e003:f12] 一方、欧州は競争激化などで同14.6%減の6万4000台、その他市場は中東情勢の悪化で同16.8%減の9万1000台と落ち込んでいる。 [e003:f13] 一方で通期見通しについては、第1四半期の販売がほぼ横ばいだったことに加え、中国市場の需要減と中東情勢の混乱継続を見込み、グローバル販売台数と生産台数を期初発表からそれぞれ15万台下方修正し、主要財務指標は据え置いている。 [e003:f14] 三菱自動車：中東影響下でも増収増益、新型「パジェロ」で反攻 三菱自動の売上高は前年同期比2%増の6199億円、営業利益は同80%増の101億円、経常利益は同102%増の97億円、四半期純利益は同100%増の14億円と、中東情勢の逆風下でも増収増益を実現している。 [e003:f15] 通期見通しは第1四半期実績を踏まえて期初見通しを据え置き、売上高3兆2600億円（前期比13%増）、営業利益900億円（同19%増）、当期純利益250億円（同150%増）を見込む。 [e003:f16] 通期業績見通しは前回予想から修正され、売上収益は前回比1000億円増の6兆9000億円（前期比9.6%増）へ上方修正された一方、営業利益は前回比300億円減の5400億円（前期比13.3%減）へ下方修正されている。

【ジョイフル本田 FY2026 FY 決算説明会】営業利益18.8%減も「負ののれん」で純利益増、20円増配を発表─来期は本業回復なるか
evidence.body: [e005:f01] ジョイフル本田が発表した2026年6月期連結決算は、売上高1328億1700万円（前期比3.0％増）ながら、営業利益は87億3200万円と前期比18.8％の大幅減。 [e005:f02] 一方、ホンダ取得に伴う負ののれん発生益19億4000万円の特別利益計上で、親会社株主帰属純利益は90億200万円と8.1％増益を確保した。 [e005:f03] 既存店は上期に防災特需の反動や客数減で低迷したが、第4四半期に中東情勢を背景としたナフサ由来商品の需要が17.5億円押し上げ、通期では前年並みに着地。 [e005:f04] 来期予想は売上高1400億円と増収を見込むものの、のれん益剥落で純利益は66億円へ減る見通し。 [e005:f05] ジョイフル本田、営業利益18.8％減——のれん益で純利益は増も、本業の重石浮き彫りに 「人材への投資は将来の利益創出に不可欠」——平山社長が語った先行投資の論理と、石炭化学特需という偶発的追い風 ジョイフル本田（3191）が8月10日に開いた2026年6月期決算説明会で、同社の置かれた苦しい収益構造が浮かび上がった。 [e005:f06] 連結売上高は1328億1700万円と前期比3.0％増を確保したが、営業利益は87億3200万円と同18.8％の大幅減。 [e005:f07] 純利益は子会社取得に伴う負ののれん発生益19億4000万円を特別利益に計上し、90億200万円（前期比8.1％増）と見かけ上の増益を保った。 [e005:f08] 2026年6月期は株式会社ホンダを2025年12月20日みなし取得日として連結） CFOの久保氏は「人材投資、新規出店に伴う費用、株式会社ホンダの連結化に伴うコスト増が主な要因」と説明。 [e005:f09] 専門店出店とホンダ買収、成長の種を蒔く 2026年6月期に新規出店した専門店は7店舗。 [e005:f10] 2026年6月期の営業利益はマイナス2.3％と赤字だったが、基幹システム統一、セルフレジ導入、仕入集約などの統合効果を急ぎ、2027年6月期の黒字化を目標に掲げる。 [e005:f11] さらに4月14日には、アークランズ株式会社との経営統合に関する基本合意書を締結。 [e005:f12] 来期予想と配当——一過性利益の反動に要警戒 2027年6月期の連結業績予想は、売上高1400億円（前期比5.4％増）、営業利益86億円（同1.5％減）、親会社株主帰属純利益66億円（同26.7％減）と、売上拡大と本業利益の伸び悩みが並存する内容。 [e005:f13] 純利益の減少は、今期計上した負ののれん発生益19.4億円の剥落が主因で、経営陣は「一過性」との認識を示す。 [e005:f14] 販管費は431億円とさらに増加を見込む。 [e005:f15] DX面では2027年6月期中にシステム開発を進め、28年6月期中の運用開始を目指す。 [e005:f16] 株主還元では、今期の年間配当を84円（中間42円、期末42円）と前期から20円増配した。

資材・プロ用品、ガーデンファームが専門店出店効果とナフサ需要で大きく伸長 売上総利益率は住宅着工件数減少による資材売上減、価格競争力維持のため低下 定番商品は仕入価格上昇を踏まえ価格改定を実施 出店・改装 専門店7店舗出店（2028年6月期までの目標20～30店舗に対し初年度計画通り） ジョイフル本田資材館が売上計画順調 荒川店ペット館を「ペッツクローバー」としてリニューアルし、3～6月の店舗全体客数が前年超え 株式会社ホンダの連結化 2025年9月30日に全株式取得、2025年12月20日を見なし取得日として連結 当期の営業利益はマイナス2.3% 基幹システム・モバイル端末・チャットツール統一、レジ入替、セルフレジ導入、キャッシュレス対応、仕入集約などを推進 2027年6月期黒字化目標 キャッシュフロー・財務 営業CF: 72億8300万円のプラスで成長投資を支援 現預金はホンダ株式取得、設備投資、長期借入金返済、配当で減少 純資産は利益の積み上げで増加 見通し 2027年6月期の連結業績予想は以下の通り。 [e006:f04] 売上高: 1400億円（既存店増収、専門店出店効果、ホンダ通期寄与） 売上総利益: 445億円、売上総利益率31.8% 販管費: evidence.title: アステモ、新社長にホンダ四輪本部長の井上勝史氏 竹内弘平社長は退任 ホンダ四輪事業の立て直しを全面支援
evidence.body: [e001:f01] 6月25日の定時株主総会と7月1日の臨時取締役会を経て正式決定する。 [e001:f02] 井上氏はホンダの欧州や中国の責任者などを経て、電動事業開発部門のトップ、昨年4月には四輪事業本部長に就いたが、6月にホンダの取締役退任が決まっていた。 [e001:f03] ホンダは日立が保有するアステモの株式21％分を取得し、出資比率を61％に引き上げて子会社化する予定でいる。 [e001:f04] 電気自動車（EV）戦略の失敗で業績が悪化している同社は、ソフトウエア・デファインド・ビークル（SDV）やハイブリッド車（HV）に重点を置く方針に軌道修正した。 [e001:f05] アステモはSDVや電動車向けを含むパワートレイン技術に強い。 [e001:f06] ホンダはアステモの先進技術や開発力を高く評価しており、連携を強化する。 [e001:f07] 今回、ホンダの四輪事業部門で実務経験の長い井上氏にトップ交代することで、ホンダの四輪事業の立て直しについて、系列サプライヤーとして全面的に支える体制を整える。 [e001:f08] 竹内社長もホンダ出身で、2023年7月にアステモの社長に就いた。 [e001:f09] ホンダでは財務・管理部門が長く、アステモでは前任社長時代の品質問題を踏まえた対応や財務体質の改善、株式公開に向けた準備などを担ってきた。 [e001:f10] 井上勝史氏（いのうえ・かつし）1986年3月、横浜国立大学経営学部卒、同年4月ホンダ入社。 [e001:f11] 2015年ホンダカーズインディア社長、16年ホンダ執行役員、欧州地域本部長、20年常務執行役員兼中国本部長兼本田技研工業（中国）投資総経理兼本田技研科技（中国）総経理、23年執行役専務兼電動事業開発本部長、25年取締役執行役専務兼四輪事業本部長兼リスクマネジメントオフィサー、25年6月同取締役執行役専務、26年4月同取締役。

evidence.title: Aston Martin Delays EVs To Keep The V12 Alive
evidence.body: [e001:f01] In a world where big engines are going extinct, Aston Martin is preserving the V12 for enthusiasts. [e001:f02] THE BREAKDOWN Aston Martin has found a way to keep building the V12 engine. [e001:f03] The company can produce fewer than 1,000 V12s per year. [e001:f04] Aston will delay EVs until the 2030s due to a lack of demand. [e001:f05] Future Aston models will feature improved dynamics. [e001:f06] Aston Martin is currently working on its next-generation vehicle platform, which will underpin its future sports cars and SUV models. [e001:f07] Speaking with AutoExpress, the British automaker revealed that these next-generation vehicles should continue to offer a V12 engine despite strict emissions regulations, especially in Europe. [e001:f08] "We've done some work to make the V12 compliant with European and US [regulations]," said Aston Martin CEO Adrian Hallmark. [e001:f09] "If we keep our V12 sales under 1,000 per year, then we’re exempt from legislation until 2035 at least." In other words, Aston can continue building models like the current Vanquish, and even few-offs like the One 77. [e001:f10] Instead of having four EVs by 2030, the brand will now introduce its first EVs in the 2030s. [e001:f11] The next-generation architecture will allow Aston Martin to build multiple vehicles ranging from SUVs to supercars all on the same production line. [e001:f12] That not only cuts down on costs, which is good for Aston, but it means there should be more commonality between these models, and that's great for enthusiasts. [e001:f13] Using the current models as a benchmark, the next-generation vehicles should deliver improved rigidity with more bonded aluminum, superior turn-in thanks to rear-wheel steering, and enhanced refinement from stiffer suspension mounting points. [e001:f14] Motor1's Take: The idea of a Lucid-powered Aston Martin EV sounded like a match made in heaven, but if there is no demand for such a product, it makes sense for the company to pivot. [e001:f15] There are very few V12s left on the market, so it is cool to see Aston fight to keep this configuration alive. [e001:f16] The Aston Martin Vanquish's Designer Tells Us Why It's Still So Important。

evidence.title: Honda Invests in Japanese Quantum Algorithm Startup Quemix
evidence.body: [e002:f01] The funding, provided through Honda’s global open innovation initiative, Honda Xcelerator Ventures , aims to accelerate the practical deployment of quantum computing for next-generation materials development. [e002:f02] This investment builds on an established and successful research partnership between Quemix and Honda. [e002:f03] In May 2025, the two companies jointly developed a novel quantum state readout technique, which was followed in June 2026 by a breakthrough quantum algorithm designed to exponentially accelerate Density Functional Theory calculations, a cornerstone method in computational chemistry and materials science. [e002:f04] Building on this momentum, Quemix plans to leverage its advanced algorithm technologies to transition quantum methods from experimental research directly into practical automotive materials development processes. [e002:f05] The primary initial focus will be accelerating the development of next-generation battery materials to support Honda’s long-term goal of achieving carbon neutrality by 2050. [e002:f06] Established in 2019, Quemix specializes in algorithms for fault-tolerant quantum computing and computational materials science. [e002:f07] The company holds patents for Probabilistic Imaginary-Time Evolution, a quantum chemistry calculation algorithm with mathematically proven acceleration, and is targeting full commercial applicability in materials simulation by 2030. [e002:f08] Automotive manufacturers continue to be active early adopters of quantum computing for electrochemistry and battery simulation. [e002:f09] Honda’s direct equity stake in Quemix deepens their technical alignment and signals a shift from exploratory joint research toward integrating domain-specific quantum software directly into industrial materials development workflows. [e002:f10] Additional details can be reviewed via the original press releases published on the official Quemix website. [e002:f11] For additional details, read the original press releases from Quemix or review their past joint technical announcements on quantum readout and accelerated DFT algorithms .
